thesis: The podcast argues that the largest US technology companies are building massive AI infrastructure at a conservative estimated annual capex of $400 billion, effectively bearing the cost of the buildout while input costs for accessing models have fallen over 99% and capabilities have doubled every seven months. The speakers posit that AI will evolve into a utility like electricity or Wi-Fi, creating a new surplus where approximately 90% of the value accrues to end customers and only 10% is captured by companies, thereby expanding the total market opportunity beyond previous software cycles.
